Job Title : Assistant Manager Factory Logistics & Operational Excellence

Job Location : Cikarang Factory

About Unilever

With 3.4 billion people in over 190 countries using our products every day, Unilever is a business that makes a real impact on the world. Work on brands that are loved and improve the lives of our consumers and the communities around us. We are driven by our purpose: to make sustainable living commonplace, and it is our belief that doing business the right way drives superior performance. At the heart of what we do is our people – we believe that when our people work with purpose, we will create a better business and a better world.

At Unilever, your career will be a unique journey, grounded in our inclusive, collaborative, and flexible working environment. We don’t believe in the ‘one size fits all’ approach and instead we will equip you with the tools you need to shape your own future.

Job Purpose

Lead end-to-end factory logistics, warehouse, case erecting, palletizer and future inhouse banded operations—including third-party service providers and internal teams—to consistently meet safety, quality, productivity, and cost targets.

Ensure high inventory accuracy, timely material flow, waste reduction, and accurate SAP governance, including month-end production closing. Maintain strict regulatory and internal compliance (BRCGS, ISO 9001, SJPH, CCPKRTB, 5S) as well as equipment safety certification as the site's MMHE Competent Person.

Drive continuous operational improvement and cross-functional collaboration to optimize end-to-end supply chain efficiency and cost performance.

Main Responsibilities

Third-Party Operations & Performance Management

• Manage third-party service providers supporting warehouse, case erecting, palletizer operations and future banded inhouse operations, ensuring agreed productivity, quality, safety, cost and service standards are consistently achieved.
• Define, monitor, and regularly review KPIs and productivity performance of third-party operations, and drive corrective actions and continuous improvement initiatives where required.
• Review third-party cost structures and operational spending to identify and implement productivity improvements and production cost-saving opportunities.
• Ensure third-party providers conduct regular internal training to maintain required competency standards in productivity, quality, and safety.
• Ensure preventive and corrective maintenance of operational assets, including both company-owned and rental equipment, is executed according to agreed maintenance plans.
• Manage workforce requirements and overtime arrangements, ensuring output-based manpower requirements are calculated and planned appropriately.

Warehouse & Material Management

• Ensure warehouse unloading turnaround time (TAT) meets the agreed Service Level Agreement (SLA) through effective coordination and operational control.
• Maintain warehouse inventory accuracy in accordance with agreed SLA by ensuring all material receiving, storage, system transactions, and inventory-control procedures are properly executed.
• Lead quarterly stock-taking activities in collaboration with the Finance Controller team, ensuring accurate inventory reconciliation and timely resolution of discrepancies.
• Review RM/PM aging inventory with Planning and Quality teams and ensure agreed action plans are implemented and followed through.
• Ensure all Raw Materials (RM) and Packaging Materials (PM) stored in the warehouse have valid Safety Data Sheets (SDS/MSDS) and appropriate GHS labeling.
• Ensure material write-off activities are executed in accordance with applicable procedures and approval requirements.

Production Material Control, Waste & SAP Governance

• Supervise RM/PM Team Leaders and Controllers, ensuring effective execution of material-control and production-support activities.
• Review site production waste and ensure agreed waste-reduction action plans are implemented within the committed timeline.
• Ensure accurate and timely month-end production closing, including resolution of SAP transaction errors and outstanding material movements.
• Ensure material master data is accurately maintained and updated in accordance with established procedures and governance requirements.
• Ensure production and material-control transactions are accurately executed in SAP to support reliable inventory and production reporting.

Safety, Quality & Regulatory Compliance

• Ensure warehouse, case erecting, and palletizer operations comply with applicable BRCGS, SJPH, ISO 9001, CCPKRTB, and internal operational requirements.
• Drive effective implementation and sustainability of 5S workplace standards across the responsible operational areas.
• Follow up and drive closure of Safety and Quality findings within warehouse, case erecting, and palletizer areas.
• Conduct regular reviews of operational equipment to ensure it remains safe, compliant, and fit for use, including monitoring the validity of required inspection and certification status.
• Act as the site's MMHE Competent Person, ensuring Material Movement and Handling Equipment is appropriately inspected, maintained, operated, and certified as safe and fit for use.
• Maintain and periodically review Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), Work Instructions (WIs), and Risk Assessments applicable to warehouse, case erecting, and palletizer operations.

Continuous Improvement & Cross-Functional Collaboration

• Analyze operational performance, losses, productivity, and cost drivers to identify and implement continuous improvement and cost-saving opportunities.
• Coordinate with Production, Planning, Quality, Safety, Engineering, Procurement, and Finance functions to resolve operational issues and improve end-to-end material flow.
• Drive corrective and preventive actions arising from operational, safety, quality, inventory, and equipment-related findings, ensuring actions are completed within agreed timelines.

Requirements

• University degree in engineering disciplines
• Preferable have 1 year experience in Factory Logistics and RMS operation
• Have understanding in SAP process.

Curious about what it’s really like to work at Unilever? Explore our Life at Unilever : Search our Job Opportunities at Unilever and meet the people shaping our culture.

Unilever is an organisation committed to equity, inclusion and diversity to drive our business results and create a better future, every day, for our diverse employees, global consumers, partners, and communities. We believe a diverse workforce allows us to match our growth ambitions and drive inclusion across the business. At Unilever we are interested in every individual bringing their ‘Whole Self’ to work and this includes you! Thus if you require any support or access requirements, we encourage you to advise us at the time of your application so that we can support you through your recruitment journey.

Chandra Asri Group is a leading chemical and infrastructure solutions company in Indonesia with a track record of over 31 years in the petrochemical industry. The company employs over 2,000 dedicated staff, incorporates state-of-the art technologies and supporting facilities located strategically in the country’s industrial hub, Cilegon and Serang. As a Growth Partner, Chandra Asri is committed on creating high-value jobs, expanding the domestic petrochemical value chain, and serving the needs of the vibrant and growing Indonesian market. Chandra Asri is currently expanding its portfolio in the energy sector and incorporating its asset as well as operational infrastructure to supports the expansion plan of the second world-scale integrated petrochemical complex in Indonesia, CAP2.
Responsibilities :

• Shall act as the Company's focal point for the development and implementation of the Port Facility Security Management System in coordination with the appointed Recognized Security Organization (RSO).
• Lead and coordinate the preparation of the Port Facility Security Assessment (PFSA).
• Review and validate PFSA findings, security risks, and recommended mitigation measures proposed by the RSO.
• Coordinate the development, review, and finalization of the Port Facility Security Plan (PFSP).
• Ensure PFSP is practical, operationally effective, and aligned with terminal operations.
• Coordinate security gap assessments during engineering, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness phases.
• Monitor RSO project progress, deliverables, schedules, and quality of work.
• Review technical reports, drawings, and recommendations submitted by the RSO.
• Coordinate multidisciplinary meetings involving Marine Operations, Security, HSE, Engineering, Operations, and Project teams during PFSA/PFSP development.
• Ensure all security measures recommended by the RSO are technically feasible and incorporated into facility design and operational procedures.
• Coordinate implementation of corrective actions arising from PFSA recommendations.
• Support budget preparation for ISPS implementation, including security infrastructure, systems, equipment, training, and manpower.
• Coordinate pre-verification activities prior to regulatory inspections.
• Facilitate verification by the Directorate General of Sea Transportation and other competent authorities for Statement of Compliance of a Port Facility (SoCPF).
• Coordinate closure of findings raised during verification and certification processes.
• Maintain communication with the RSO throughout the project lifecycle and ensure timely completion of all contractual deliverables.

Qualification :

• Minimum Bachelor Degree in one of the following disciplines: Marine Transportation, Nautical Science, Marine Engineering, Maritime Studies, and all Engineering disciplines.
• Minimum 3 years of relevant experience in Port Operation (TUKS or Tersus)
• Mandatory Certified Port Facility Security Officer (PFSO) IMO Model Course 3.21
• Have expert knowledge about vessel operations, as well as the associated Port operations.
• Good English communication skills, spoken and written.
• Proficient in Microsoft Office

This position will be placed at Site Office Cilegon
